NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and the continuing state of emergency, including masking
  and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held
  remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public
  may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 824 8053 6666 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 824 8053 6666, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 26, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:02 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64434 THROUGH 64444 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $32,184.87 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100221 THROUGH 100321
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $80,619.65 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $112,804.52 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 26, 2021
 D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 12, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 736 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 10.44 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF BICYCLES, ELECTRIC BICYCLES,
  AND MOTORIZED BICYCLES

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 736 for a first reading.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Attorney Davis explained that human-propelled bicycles will be permitted on the multi-use
pathway along Palos Verdes Drive North, as well as in the bike lane on the street, but motorized
and electric bikes will be prohibited, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

City Manager Grammer added that public education and outreach campaigns with the schools
and community would be put in place to inform them of the new requirements, including
proposed signage that would be reviewed by the Traffic & Safety Committee.

Management Analyst Slawson reported that the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has
been notified about this proposed Ordinance, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that all bicycles are prohibited on horse trails. He
discussed in detail the differences between the various classes of electric bicycles (e-bikes) on
the market. He suggested staff further research the option of classifying class 1 e-bikes in the
same category as human-propelled bikes.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN expressed concern regarding regular bikes and class 1 e-bikes on
sidewalks with pedestrians.

Discussion ensued regarding the uses of e-bikes and the potential speeds that can be reached
by the different classes of e-bikes and human-propelled bikes.

City Attorney Davis noted that all three classes of e-bikes were included in the proposed
Ordinance. He also noted that if the classes were regulated differently within the Ordinance, it
may make enforcement more difficult as recognizing the different classes may be challenging.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that class 1 and class 2 e-bikes have throttles which
can be recognized by the enforcement agency.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern about public confusion if some classes
were prohibited and other were not.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 26, 2021
 Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the current code prohibits riding bikes in parks other
than on driveways, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Staff confirmed the City does not have any designated mountain bike trails, in response to
MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN confirmed that the proposed Ordinance would allow for e-
bikes to continue to be used in all locations that regular bikes are allowed.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN brought up a discussion about e-bike use among students and safety
concerns.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested staff contact the Dapplegray Elementary School
Principal and Rancho Vista Elementary School Principal to inform them of the Ordinance which
may impact their students.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 736 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 10.44 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF BICYCLES,
  ELECTRIC BICYCLES, AND MOTORIZED BICYCLES.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 736 by title.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN allowed for public comment to be heard by the following resident
out of order:

Public comment received by resident John Tayeks regarding Waste Management rates.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

B.  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 737 ESTABLISHING
  CHAPTER 12.10 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF SIDEWALK VENDING

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 737 for a first reading.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Attorney Davis noted that the City has not faced the issue of overcrowding of street
vendors, and that this Ordinance ultimately is aiming to protect the business community
while accepting State law that allows for this activity on public property, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

City Attorney Davis explained that food vendors would need appropriate permits from Los
Angeles County, and that all vendors would need a business license through the City, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

City Attorney Davis explained that the City does not regulate any required permits beyond
the City’s business licenses, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 26, 2021
 Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 737 ESTABLISHING
  CHAPTER 12.10 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO THE REGULATION OF SIDEWALK VENDING.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 737 by title.

C.  MEASURE A COMPETITIVE GRANT APPLICATION RESOLUTIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2488 and Resolution
  No. 2489 to approve applications for Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open
  Space District’s Measure A Competitive Grants Programs for the George F Canyon
  Nature Center project in the amount of $1,000,000 and the Butcher Park project in
  the amount of $100,000 and authorize staff to submit grant applications accordingly.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2488 AND RESOLUTION NO. 2489 TO APPROVE
  APPLICATIONS FOR LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGIONAL PARK AND OPEN
  SPACE DISTRICT’S MEASURE A COMPETITIVE GRANTS PROGRAMS FOR
  THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $1,000,000 AND THE BUTCHER PARK PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $100,000 AND AUTHORIZE STAFF TO SUBMIT GRANT APPLICATIONS
  ACCORDINGLY.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution 2488 and Resolution 2489 by title.

D.  CONTRACT FOR REMOVAL AND UPGRADED VINYL FENCING AT HIGHRIDGE
  PARK

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a contract in the amount of $52,800
  to Valley Cities Gonzales Fence, Inc. for the removal and installation of a new,
  upgraded vinyl fence at Highridge Park, approved as to form by the City Attorney,
  and authorize a budget adjustment in the total amount of $60,000 using Park Facilities
  Fees toward this project

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Attorney Davis explained the State requirement of prevailing wages, which applies to
all of the City’s public works projects, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if it was possible to require the vinyl fencing be made from
recycled materials, and also that it be UV resistant. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commended
staff for including pathways throughout the fencing to prevent people from climbing over.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 26, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested staff explore options for recycling the old fence
materials that are to be removed.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A CONTRACT IN THE AMOUNT OF $52,800 TO VALLEY CITIES
  GONZALES FENCE, INC. FOR THE REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION OF A
  NEW, UPGRADED VINYL FENCE AT HIGHRIDGE PARK, APPROVED AS TO
  FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY, AND AUTHORIZE A BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENT IN THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF $60,000 USING PARK
  FACILITIES FEES TOWARD THIS PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 735 ADDING
  CHAPTER 8.40 (REGULATION OF SMOKING) TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 735 for a first reading.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Public testimony was received from Nelly Munoz, Christine Mae Guanzing, and Linus, all in
favor of the proposed ordinance. Christine Mae Guanzing urged the Council to reconsider a
comprehensive smoking Ordinance.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated he strongly agreed that the City should adopt a comprehensive
smoking Ordinance at a later date when the burdens of the pandemic are no longer impacting
local businesses, and suggested this be revisited by the Council after a reasonable amount of
time.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 735 ADDING CHAPTER
  8.40 (REGULATION OF SMOKING) TO THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 735 by title.

B.  PROPOSAL FROM E.C. CONSTRUCTION FOR ADDITIONAL WORK TO REPAIR
  STORM DRAIN ON HAWTHORNE BLVD

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve an amendment to the Public Works
  Contract with E.C. Construction (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to complete
  the storm drain repair on Hawthorne Blvd. under the project supervision of Willdan
  Engineering in the amount of $59,080, plus a $15,000 contingency, for a grand total of
  $74,080.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 26, 2021
 Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained the urgency of the
storm drain repair with the rainy season beginning October 15, and noted that a more
extensive hydrology study would be needed to explore other options, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba discussed options for the
excavated dirt, in response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO THE PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH
  E.C. CONSTRUCTION (ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY), TO COMPLETE THE STORM DRAIN REPAIR ON
  HAWTHORNE BLVD. UNDER THE PROJECT SUPERVISION OF WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING IN THE AMOUNT OF $59,080, PLUS A $15,000
  CONTINGENCY, FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $74,080.

  AYES:  Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

C.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that booster doses of the COVID-19 vaccine are now
available for eligible groups for all three available vaccines, and that Pfizer, Moderna, and
Johnson and Johnson doses can now be mixed.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas reported that this weekend's Concert in the Park and
Prepared Peninsula Expo were both a success. Upcoming events include the 42nd annual
Tracy Austin Double Tennis Tournament on November 12 – 14, the annual Parade of Lights
on December 4, and a Holiday House Decorating Contest later in December.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF participated in the Equestrian Committee meeting this week,
where an emergency alert platform through Everbridge was discussed, as well as an
upcoming equine microchipping event.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on the League of California Cities’ Leaders Workshop
that she attended virtually, where the League’s strategic priorities for 2022 were discussed.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported on the League of California Cities’ Transportation,
Communications and Public Works Committee’s consideration of AB 122 which would have
allowed bicyclists to pause, not stop, at stop signs. This bill was passed by both houses but
vetoed by Governor Newsom.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN announced the Environmental Advisory Committee meeting
tomorrow evening, October 27.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

OCTOBER 26, 2021
 13.  CLOSED SESSION

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:40 pm MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
City Council meeting on Tuesday, November 9, 2021, at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a
Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor
